description: Whether a value satisfies or fails the contract an operation's input or output schema states, read as JSON Schema 2020-12 with format as an annotation, pattern values and patternProperties names as ECMA-262 regular expressions with Unicode semantics, and references resolved as section 7 defines; or whether the result is undefined, rests on a resource the document does not contain, or meets no contract because none is stated (section 5.2, Value contracts).

scenarios.description: Extension fields on an operation do not change its input contract (section 12).
A pattern is part of the input contract: a string of digits satisfies it and a string of letters fails it (section 5.2).
unevaluatedProperties: false is part of the input contract: an object with an undeclared member fails it (section 5.2).
A recursive schema that consumes the instance as it recurses has a defined result: a finite matching value satisfies it (sections 5.2 and 7.4).
A recursive object schema that consumes the instance as it recurses has a defined result: a finite value that does not match fails it (sections 5.2 and 7.4).
Mutual recursion between two schemas keeps its meaning (section 7.4).
Inside a schema that declares $id, # names that schema (section 7.5), so a tree recurses through it.
A pointer that reaches a schema declaring $id identifies that schema (section 7.3); these values never reach the recursion inside it.
A value valid against the input schema satisfies the contract (section 5.2).
A value invalid against the input schema fails the contract (section 5.2).
format is an annotation in a value contract (section 5.2), so a string that is not an email address satisfies format: email.
A value contract applies to each value separately, never to several values taken together (section 5.2).
A reference to a URI that an $id in the document declares resolves within the document (section 7), so the contract needs no outside resource.
Same-document references resolve against the OBI document when a value is evaluated (sections 7.2 and 7.3).
An absent input states no value contract, so a value neither satisfies nor fails one (section 5.2).
An absent output states no value contract, so a value neither satisfies nor fails one (section 5.2).
input: true is a stated contract every value satisfies (section 5.1).
input: false is a stated contract no value satisfies (section 5.1).
Where a value's result depends on a resource the document does not contain, the document alone does not settle it (section 5.2).

A string satisfies anyOf through its first branch whatever the external branch gives; a number's result rests on the external resource (section 5.2). Software that evaluates the whole schema may decline the first.
A cycle that recurses without consuming any of the instance has an undefined result (section 7.4).
Within an $id resource, a pointer that reaches no schema has an undefined result (section 7.4).
Within an $id resource, a plain name declared twice has an undefined result (section 7.4).
An inline modifier group is not an ECMA-262 (11th edition) pattern, so the result is undefined (section 5.2).
An identity escape the u flag forbids is not a valid pattern, so the result is undefined (section 5.2).
An invalid patternProperties name makes the result undefined wherever it applies (section 5.2).
ECMA-262 \s matches Unicode white space and line terminators.
ECMA-262 \d matches ASCII digits only.
With the u flag, . matches one code point outside the Basic Multilingual Plane.
$ matches only at the end of input, not before a trailing newline.
A pattern is not anchored: it matches anywhere in the string.
patternProperties names are ECMA-262 patterns with Unicode semantics.
A Unicode property escape matches under the u flag (section 5.2).
OpenAPI 3.0's nullable is an unknown keyword under 2020-12 (section 5.2).
The legacy dependencies keyword is not a 2020-12 assertion: the 2020-12 meta-schema keeps it only to validate its form.
Content keywords are annotations under 2020-12 (JSON Schema Validation, content vocabulary).
A plain name declared in the document resource identifies the schema that declares it (section 7.3).
A fragment is percent-decoded once, so a percent-encoded plain name identifies the schema that declares the decoded name (section 7.3).
A percent-encoded JSON Pointer is decoded before it is evaluated (section 7.3).
A relative reference inside an $id resource resolves against its base (section 7.2).
A $dynamicRef inside an $id resource resolves through the dynamic scope to the document resource's $dynamicAnchor (section 7.5).
An array schema applies to each value, never to the values as one array (section 5.2).
With the external resource the case supplies, the result is what JSON Schema gives with that resource (section 5.2).
format: regex is an annotation, separate from the pattern keyword.
An example outside the schema does not widen the contract (section 5.1).
Examples do not narrow the contract to themselves (section 5.1).
An example does not change an enum's contract (section 5.1).

anyOf's result rests on the first branch's type alone, whatever the second branch's invalid pattern gives: a string satisfies it and a number fails it (section 5.2). Software that evaluates the whole schema may decline.
A value that lacks the property satisfies the contract whatever the property schema's invalid pattern gives (section 5.2). Software that evaluates the whole schema may decline.
Numbers are compared at their exact value (section 5): 2^53 + 1 is not 2^53.
multipleOf is decided on exact decimal values, the arbitrary-precision numbers of JSON Schema's data model (section 5.2; JSON Schema Core section 4.2.1).
An external schema follows the dialect JSON Schema assigns it (section 5.2): the supplied resource declares draft-07, where dependencies asserts.
A percent-encoded pointer is decoded before lookup even when the literal spelling also names a property: my%20type means 'my type' (section 7.3).
A modifier group (?i:...) is not a pattern under the pinned ECMA-262 11th edition (section 13.1), so the result is undefined (section 5.2), even where a newer engine accepts it.
Within an $id resource, a pointer that reaches a map rather than a schema has an undefined result (section 7.4).
A reference to a URI that an $id in the document declares resolves within the document (section 7): an $id that claims the 2020-12 meta-schema's URI names the document's schema, not the meta-schema.
Inside an $id resource, a $ref that is not a well-formed URI-reference (a raw space) has an undefined result (section 7.4).
\p{EBase} names no property in the pinned ECMA-262 11th edition (section 13.1; ECMA-262 section 21.2.1.1, Table 56): the pattern is invalid, so the result is undefined (section 5.2).
Script=Kawi is not a script value in the pinned ECMA-262 11th edition (section 13.1; ECMA-262 Table 58): the pattern is invalid, so the result is undefined (section 5.2).
ECMA-262's dot matches no line terminator: not \n, \r, U+2028, or U+2029.
Without the i flag, ECMA-262's \w is ASCII only, even with the u flag: neither e with an acute accent nor the Kelvin sign is a word character.
ECMA-262's \b is a boundary between an ASCII word character and anything else, so a letter outside ASCII ends a word.
With the u flag, an escaped surrogate pair is one code point, so a class holding it matches the one character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane.
A schema nested in an $id resource that declares $id of its own is a resource too, resolved against its parent's base (section 7.2): https://e.example.test/inner.json names it.
A 2020-12 $schema at an input that declares no $id, where JSON Schema does not permit $schema, names the dialect the schema is already read in and has no other effect (section 5.2).

Validity can depend on an undefined result through annotations: unevaluatedProperties counts b as evaluated only if the branch holding the invalid pattern is valid, so an object with a and b has an undefined result. Without b, or with a property no branch evaluates, every way the pattern could come out gives the same validity (section 5.2). Software that evaluates the whole schema may decline those.
Annotations from a supplied resource count: the resource's properties evaluate a, so unevaluatedProperties holds for an object with a alone and fails for one that adds b (section 5.2).
Without the resource, whether its annotations evaluate a is unknown, so the result rests on the resource (section 5.2).

The value-contract provisions hold inside a supplied resource: format is an annotation, a pattern is read with Unicode semantics, so the dot matches one code point outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, and the resource's own reference resolves as JSON Schema defines (section 5.2).

Under oneOf, a string's validity depends on the invalid pattern whatever the absent resource holds, so its result is undefined; a number, which the pattern ignores, depends on the resource alone, so its result rests on it (section 5.2).
Under allOf, the absent resource could reject the string whatever the invalid pattern gives, so the result is not undefined for every resource and rests on the resource (section 5.2).
With the resource supplied and rejecting the string, the invalid pattern no longer matters, so the string fails (section 5.2). Software that evaluates the whole schema may decline.
With the resource supplied and accepting the string, validity depends on the invalid pattern, so the result is undefined (section 5.2).
A supplied resource whose root declares no $schema is read as 2020-12, so its dependentRequired, which draft-07 does not define, applies: a value with a but not b fails (section 5.2).

An embedded resource without $schema takes its enclosing resource's dialect, as JSON Schema defines (Core section 9.3.2); only where JSON Schema leaves the dialect to the implementation is it read as 2020-12 (section 5.2). Here the supplied root declares draft-07, so the embedded resource's dependencies asserts and a value with a but not b fails.

Which schema a $ref reaches is one of the ways an undefined result can come out, beside whether the reference comes out valid at all: a plain name declared twice in an $id resource gives two targets with the same validity but different annotations, so an object with x depends on which one unevaluatedProperties sees, and an empty object on whether the reference comes out valid (section 5.2). With a property neither target evaluates, every way gives the same validity, invalid. Software that evaluates the whole schema may decline that one.
